A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same evolving TrendFact/FactISR research despite the changed title and substantial revision. All pages, tables, figures and equations are readable. V1 has no appendix; v2 includes readable appendices A–C. Changed experimental conditions limit direct performance comparisons, not document comparability.

before.justification: V1 reports original verification and explanation-generation experiments in Tables 2–3, an iteration study in Figure 4, and a correction case in Figure 5.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark evaluations and component ablations in Tables 2–3, plus a reward-decoding case study in Appendix C.

M1.justification: V1's FactISR uses cross-validated pseudo-explanation generation, multitask fine-tuning, and repeated explanation revision with similarity-based stopping. V2 replaces this procedure with a six-step evidence-triangulation prompt and token-triggered, decaying reward decoding that encourages reflection. This is a substantive algorithm replacement, not merely renaming self-revision.

E1.justification: Chinese verification and explanation generation retain the same broad domains, reasoning requirements and 2020–2024 collection window. Trend sourcing broadens from Weibo to multiple platforms. CHEF-EG is incorporated into the consolidated TrendFact benchmark rather than losing its underlying coverage; increased sample counts alone do not establish new tasks.

E2.justification: V2 actually evaluates PROGRAMFC and CLAIMDECOMP, previously only cited, and adds DeepSeek-V3, DeepSeek-R1, o1-preview and QwQ/CoT comparisons. V1's BERT-family, Baichuan, Yi, GLM, Claude, LoRA and DPO comparisons disappear. GPT-4o and the Qwen 72B comparator remain, but the overall comparator set is substantially replaced.

E3.justification: Separate CHEF-EG and TrendFact experiments become a consolidated benchmark evaluation, with trend-derived data increasing from 2,000 to 6,512 entries. FactISR's experimental backbone changes from fine-tuned 7B/9B models to QwQ-32B. Precision, recall and ROUGE-1/2 are added, while GPT-4-based G-Eval is replaced by GPT-4o-based ECS. V2 does not retain v1's explicit split specification.

E4.justification: V1's self-revision training/iteration sweep and Macau correction example are removed. V2 instead tests incremental evidence triangulation and reward-based reflection in Tables 2–3 and adds a cold-wave example contrasting reflection with premature termination in Appendix C. These analyses address different components and failure mechanisms.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V1's five-fold procedure generates training pseudo-explanations; it is not an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: The separate benchmark results and iteration findings in v1 are substantially replaced. V1 reports Qwen2-7B+ISR at 63.79 F1 on its TrendFact test set; v2 reports QwQ+ET+ISR at 72.44 F1 and 0.8954 ECS on the consolidated benchmark. These involve different models and data, so they do not establish a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: V1's formal specification of training objectives and recursive explanation updates is replaced by v2's conditional reward-decoding rule with geometrically decaying rewards in Equation 1. Appendix A additionally defines ECS through five correctness/consistency categories normalized to 0.2–1.0. The mathematical specification changes substantially, although neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from two datasets and a unified fine-tuned self-revision framework to a consolidated benchmark, a new explanation metric, and enhancement of reasoning models. V2's abstract, introduction and conclusion emphasize temporal relevance and limitations of leading reasoning models. The overarching non-English explanation-generation novelty claim remains.

C2.justification: V1's explanations concerning DPO failures, iteration-induced evidence loss and early stopping are replaced by interpretations of reasoning models' concise final outputs, information retained in reasoning traces, and premature reflection termination. V2 also explicitly identifies manual claim rewriting, evidence collection and explanation annotation as costly limitations in Section 7.

D1.justification: V2 adds the complete Chinese/English prompt in Appendix B, reward-decoding settings and ECS scoring details, replacing v1's LoRA and two-stage training configuration. It also changes the disclosed annotation-team size. A future code-release promise becomes a specific statement and repository link for code and data availability; external availability was not verified.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially refocused toward benchmark sources, explanation annotations and reasoning models. V2 adds discussions and citations including FEVEROUS, AVeriTeC, QuanTemp, X-Fact and DeepSeek-R1, plus a benchmark comparison table. Much of v1's positioning around training methods and earlier verification architectures is removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, method narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten around the benchmark contribution. Dataset construction is reorganized, the method appears under a new Baselines section, and numbered sections, a limitations section and appendices A–C replace v1's simpler unnumbered structure.

P2.justification: V2 incorporates the retained Forbidden City example into a new construction/distribution overview and redraws the method diagram. The split table and iteration plots disappear; result tables are restructured for one benchmark and new metrics. A benchmark comparison table, ECS rubric, full-prompt figure and replacement case-study figure substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful task-specific comparators, a complete prompt, an explicit ECS rubric and code/data access information. However, it removes v1's explicit evaluation splits without clearly identifying the evaluated subset, and leaves aspects of reward decoding and ECS judging underspecified. Its broad component-improvement discussion also needs qualification: Table 3 shows reflection raising ECS while lowering BLEU-4 and ROUGE-2/L relative to ET alone. These benefits and reporting weaknesses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
